mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Increasing, intensifying thunderstorm development appears probable near and north of the Minnesota/Iowa border vicinity through 6-8 AM CDT. This may be accompanied by a period of increasing potential for severe hail, then, perhaps, increasing potential for strong to severe surface gusts. It is possible that this could eventually require a severe weather watch, though it is not yet clear that this will be needed in the near term.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Downstream of stronger lingering convection developing southeastward near/northeast of the Huron SD vicinity, models have been suggesting that forcing for ascent associated with the subtle digging short wave perturbation may increasingly couple with lift driven by warm advection/convergence on the nose of a lingering 30-40 kt nocturnally strengthened southerly low-level jet. By 11-13Z, it appears this will become focused near/north of the Minnesota/Iowa border vicinity, where a corridor of increasing moisture return above at least a shallow stable boundary-layer is likely to contribute to increasingly sizable CAPE, in the presence of strengthening cloud-bearing layer shear. As this occurs, a more notable increase and intensification of thunderstorm activity appears possible, perhaps accompanied by at least a period of increasing potential for severe hail. Subsequent upscale growth might eventually organize and become accompanied by increasing risk for damaging wind gusts, though if/how soon this occurs after daybreak remains unclear.
